outcomes: A supervisor runs a workload with one putnami serve run and hands its serve step the process environment it needs, such as a port, the URLs of the workloads it runs with and a CONFIG_DATA document, without that environment reaching anything else
The supervisor reads the session stream for the process group the workload runs in and for its readiness claims, and reads the workload's output as text on stderr
nonGoals: Starting or ordering several workloads: a supervisor such as compose requests one serve run per workload
Reading the environment from a file or a flag value: --serve-env accepts only -, stdin
Recording the environment, or the fact that a run carried one, in the session
Running a supervised serve run on a hosted or portable runner

requirements.text: --serve-env - reads one JSON object of string variables from stdin and hands them to the process of each serve-workload step: a selected project's uncacheable serve step that no planned job depends on. A finite step of the same pipeline, a dependency's step, the job context, a param, a cache key, the output and the session never receive them. The flag is a job-only global flag, refused on an extension subcommand, a hosted or portable run, and a plan without a serve-workload step.

A run is refused as a usage error before any step starts when a serve-workload step's task declares in its own manifest env a variable the document sets, because the task's env would replace it. A name in the PUTNAMI_ namespace, a repeated name, a value that is not a string, a document over 1 MiB and a stdin that is a character device, such as a terminal, are refused the same way. A refusal names the variable, the task and the project, never a value.

A ready task:event is a priority record of the bounded session stream, in Go and TypeScript alike: it is admitted from the failure reserve, so a workload whose ordinary records spent their partition still delivers its claim live. A serve step's process event is a priority record for the same reason. The reserve is shared with every failure-priority record and bounded: 256 records and 256 KiB in normal mode, 2048 records and 2 MiB in verbose mode. A ready or process event that arrives once the run's failure-priority records spent it is elided from the live stream, counted in machineOutput.elided.failure and kept in the session artifact. With --output=jsonl and --serve-env, stdout carries the session stream unchanged and stderr carries the serve steps' output as putnami serve renders it in text mode.

The job runner emits one task:event of type process for each serve-workload step it starts, before any event the step writes: group is the process group the step runs in and leaderStart the start time of its leader, which a reused pid reads differently. A finite step emits none, and a producer line of type process is dropped.

Under watch, a serve run with --port 0 waits between restarts on the port of the last ready claim that announced one, the first http or https endpoint, else the first endpoint; before any claim it waits on nothing. A pinned port waits on that port and a run without a port parameter on the default port, and neither consults a claim.
